title: Cobalt Row
text:
Cobalt Row

notes:
Inbound SMB lead via self-serve signup (trial credits used). Early discovery; dev team reported latency pain from day 1. Mostly public cloud footprint; initial calls from CTO + lead eng.

Summary of current setup:
- Using Hosted API default region: us-west-2 (picked automatically on signup).
- Workloads: chat-based product recommendation widget + periodic embedding index updates.
- Traffic: low volume during POC (~20 reqs/min peak), expected burst during promotions.
- Model: using 'small-open-chat-v1' (hosted) to keep costs down.

Key complaints / observations from customer:
- "Users complain it's slow when they are in EU" (direct quote from CTO).
- p95 observed from their browser telemetry: ~480ms for US users, ~1.8s for EU users (they proxy through frontend to us-west).
- Occasional timeouts in frontend at client timeout 3s when EU traffic spikes.
- They tied perceived slowness to large prompt sizes + multiple system + conversation history tokens.

What we've already done in discovery call:
- Walked through region options in Redwood Console and explained latency tradeoffs.
- Shared quick tests: switching to eu-west reduced round-trip in our sample tests to ~220-330ms.
- Suggested obvious client-side timeout bump for POC to 6s while we tune server-side.
- Demoed streaming responses: reduced perceived latency in UX with progressive render.

Perf tuning guidance given (notes to be formalized into playbook):
- Region selection: route EU traffic to eu-west region to cut network RTT; set per-route policy in Console to route by geolocation.
- Prompt hygiene: truncate conversation history to last 3 turns + send embeddings for long context instead of full transcript. Limit max_input_tokens to 1024 for chat in POC.
- Timeouts: recommend client-side read timeout 6s for first pass; server-side request timeout 20s for long generation but use early-response streaming to improve UX.
- Streaming: enable streaming in client to render partial answers; reduces perceived latency dramatically for users.
- Batching & concurrency: for embeddings jobs, use batched requests off-peak; for chat keep concurrency low to preserve latency SLO.
- Fallbacks: set up a lightweight fallback message or cached canned responses when request exceeds 8s.
- Cost notes: reducing max_tokens and cleaning prompts reduced token usage ~18% in their sample set.

Customer constraints / priorities:
- Cost-sensitive: SMB budget, prefers minimal configuration changes.
- Wants low-friction: prefer hosted solutions, no VPC/private needed now.
- Security: needs SSO/SAML integration + SOC2 assurances before ramp but OK for POC under standard Hosted.

Proposed next actions (short):
- Deliver a 1-page perf-tuning playbook + two sample Console route configs (eu-west + us-west) and example client timeout settings (ETA: 2026-02-21).
- Schedule 30m technical session (Rohit + Ava) to walk through console routing and streaming integration.
- Provide a quick cost estimate for projected 50k tokens/mo at their recommended prompt limits.

Stubs / artifacts:
- Fireflies call: ff_2026-02-12_38b4 (30m discovery)
- Internal note: engineer ran curl tests from eu-proxy -> us-west returns SLO miss at ~1.82s (attached in RDW-1298).

CRM-style short notes (from AE):
- 2026-02-12: demo + quick perf triage; customer to try eu-west routing in Console.
- 2026-02-16: customer tried eu-west sample, saw ~250ms; asked for guidance on prompt trimming.
- 2026-02-18: follow-up email with draft playbook sent (drive link).

Quotes to include in playbook:
- "If EU users feel laggy we'll lose conversions — need a low-effort fix." — CTO
- "Keep configs simple, we don't want to manage infra." — Lead Eng

Notes on potential upsell / future:
- If switching to eu-west + streaming hits latencies targets, discuss Redwood Optimize suggestions (batching for embeddings + quantization recommendations) for cost reduction.

Internal asks for SE (Rohit):
- Provide a short sample route JSON + example SDK snippet showing streaming and timeout settings.
